But the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, rose 3.8% year-over-year in October, up from 3.6% in September and matching a three-year high set in May. Core PCE, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 3.3%, compared with economists' expectations of 3.2% and September's reading of 3.1%.
“America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock,” Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, told AFP. Consumer spending increased in dollar terms in October but was flat after adjusting for inflation.
A growing economy gives the Fed more room to raise borrowing costs to bring inflation back toward its 2% target. After Wednesday's inflation release, traders were pricing in a 98% probability of a quarter-point increase in December, according to CME FedWatch data. Today odds are set at 94%.
The Fed held rates at between 3.75% and 4% in October after raising them in September for the first time in three years. Traders are also betting on further tightening in 2027, with another increase expected as early as January.
Trump's tariffs meet another AI selloff
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative proposed tariffs targeting 14 economies, including China, the European Union, Japan and South Korea, following investigations into government policies that encourage manufacturing production beyond market demand.
The proposed rates vary by country and product, with duties of up to 20% on some Chinese imports and up to 35% on Vietnamese goods, subject to adjustments and exemptions. For the EU, the proposed 15% rate accounts for certain existing duties rather than simply adding 15 percentage points to them.
The tariffs have not taken effect, and public hearings are scheduled to begin January 25. If importers pass the additional costs on to consumers, the duties could make the Fed's job of bringing inflation down even harder.
Meanwhile, Wall Street's enthusiasm over Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia didn't last very long. The chipmaker closed Monday up 31.5% but lost more than 6% Tuesday, while Anthropic closed at $81.91, below its $83 initial public offering price less than a week after its Nasdaq debut.
Higher interest rates make it more expensive to finance data centers and reduce the present value of future earnings. Both are particularly relevant for AI companies spending heavily today in anticipation of profits years down the road.
The selloff began well before Wall Street opened. South Korea's Kospi closed 6.16% lower, while spot gold fell 2% to $3,483.59 an ounce by 9:15 a.m. ET, according to Reuters.
Crypto investors were already in bad shape before Wednesday's economic data came out. Blockchain analytics firm Glassnode reported Tuesday that Bitcoin investors were realizing their heaviest losses since the collapse of FTX and the subsequent market crash in November 2022, relative to the money that flowed into the asset over the preceding year.
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have also recorded $4.94 billion in net outflows this November through Tuesday, according to Decrypt’s ETF tracker, already making it their worst month since launching in January 2024.
The Fed's next interest rate decision is scheduled for December 9.

Japanese financial giants SBI Holdings and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) have launched launched a joint venture with the Solana Foundation to tokenize assets, develop stablecoin payment infrastructure and expand onchain financial services across Asia.
The three parties said Wednesday they had finalized agreements to transition SBI R3 Japan to new joint venture structure, with the company beginning full-scale operations as SBI Solana Global.

articles.title: Ukraine Passes Law to Legalize and Tax Its Crypto Market From July 2027
articles.text:
In brief
- Ukraine's parliament passed a law legalizing the country's crypto market and setting tax rules for virtual assets, with 271 lawmakers voting in favor.
- Crypto profits will be taxed at 18% plus a 5% military levy from July 2027, while swaps between crypto assets will not be taxed.
- The National Bank of Ukraine will oversee stablecoins and exchanges that convert crypto into cash, and can allow or ban stablecoin circulation.
Ukraine's parliament has passed a law to legalize the country's crypto market and tax virtual asset transactions, with the new rules set to take effect on July 1, 2027.
The Verkhovna Rada approved bill No. 10225-d in its second reading and as a whole on Wednesday, with 271 lawmakers voting in favor, Yaroslav Zhelezniak, first deputy chair of the parliament's finance, tax and customs committee, said on Telegram. The law still needs to be signed by President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Zhelezniak said the law would bring in an extra 15 billion hryvnias (around $330 million) in budget revenue.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
How crypto will be taxed
Under the law, individuals will pay 18% personal income tax and a 5% military levy on profits from crypto transactions, according to state news agency Ukrinform. Swapping one crypto asset for another will not be taxed, and losses from previous years can be carried forward.
For crypto bought before the law takes effect, a reduced rate will apply when holders cash out into traditional currency during 2027 and 2028: 5% plus the military levy. Zhelezniak wrote that the reduced rate would apply to "the entire volume," rather than only to profits.
Who will regulate the market
Oversight will be split between the National Securities and Stock Market Commission and the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU). The central bank will be responsible for stablecoins, and can set its own rules for their use, including allowing or banning their circulation.
The NBU will also authorize and supervise issuers of e-money tokens and providers that exchange virtual assets for traditional money, the central bank said in a statement, according to Interfax-Ukraine.

A long road to legalization
Ukraine first moved to legalize crypto in 2021, and Zelensky signed a law on virtual assets in March 2022, weeks after Russia's full-scale invasion. Soon after, the NBU banned purchases of crypto with hryvnias.
The new bill, which adds tax rules and aligns Ukraine's regulation more closely with the EU's as part of its bid for membership, passed its first reading in September 2025.
Ukraine has also explored other ways to bring crypto into the state's orbit. Lawmakers submitted a bill to create a strategic crypto reserve in June 2025, and in June 2026, the country placed more than $8.3 million in seized USDT under state management for the first time.

articles.title: Hong Kong Launches Tokenized Debt Platform With 24-Hour Settlement
articles.text:
Hong Kong launches tokenized debt platform with 24-hour settlement
The HKMA’s new platform supports settlement in multiple currencies and handles debt issuance, interest payments and repayment at maturity.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched a platform Wednesday that supports round-the-clock settlement of tokenized debt securities in multiple currencies.
The CMU Digital Asset Platform, developed and operated by CMU OmniClear Limited on behalf of the HKMA, uses cash tokens for payment and connects with conventional payment systems and central bank digital currencies.
Its onchain delivery-versus-payment model ensures that the securities and corresponding payment transfer together, or neither transfer occurs. This means the buyer receives the securities only if the seller receives payment.
The platform also handles issuance, interest payments and repayment at maturity, and supports the tokenization of existing debt securities. The HKMA said it aims to improve settlement efficiency and reduce operational costs.
The launch follows a separate expansion of Hong Kong’s digital payment infrastructure. On Nov. 2, the HKMA upgraded its Project Ensemble pilot to support 24/7 interbank settlement of tokenized deposit transactions using tokenized central bank money.
The pilot phase launched in November 2025 and initially used Hong Kong’s conventional real-time gross settlement system. Its applications have included corporate treasury management and transactions involving tokenized money market funds.

articles.title: Morning Minute: Ethereum Focuses on Security As AI Threats Rise
articles.text:
Morning Minute is a daily newsletter written by Tyler Warner. The analysis and opinions expressed are his own and do not necessarily reflect those of Decrypt. And check out our daily news show 'FOMO HOUR' covering all of the top stories and market action.
GM!
Today’s top news:
- Crypto majors selloff as AI bleeds; BTC at $58.3k
- NVDA and ANT fall 5% as stocks see deep red premarket
- Trump admin preparing tariff hikes on China, EU and 14 others
- OpenAI and ANT insiders fear next model too dangerous to release
- Ethereum doubles down on security with AI threat looming, pulls up quantum timeline
Ethereum Is Rebuilding Its Cryptography Because of AI
The Ethereum Foundation has doubled its protocol security team and made cryptography its top priority. The reason isn’t quantum computers.
Protocol lead Kev Wedderburn wrote this week that “recently AI emerged as a more urgent risk”, and the distinction matters. The quantum threat has always been a hardware problem, and hardware problems announce themselves years in advance because somebody has to build the machine. The AI version is a math problem. A sufficiently capable model could find a structural shortcut in the elliptic curve cryptography that secures Ethereum and Bitcoin, and it would need no special hardware to do it.
Researcher Justin Drake raised the scenario in October. In a worst case, he said, existing signatures could become vulnerable within months.
Then last Friday happened.
An Anthropic mathematician named Levent Alpöge posted a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, produced with an unreleased version of Claude, along with a formalized proof archive. Nobody has verified it. It doesn’t break elliptic curve cryptography and nobody is claiming it does. What it does is demonstrate the capability class Drake was describing, roughly a month after he described it.
Axios reported Tuesday that more than two dozen people familiar with internal discussions at OpenAI and Anthropic say employees worry their most advanced unreleased models may never be safe enough to release. The concerns named include reward hacking, models that hide or misrepresent their reasoning, and systems capable enough to find weaknesses in the safety measures their own developers built. OpenAI’s chief scientist proposed Sunday that labs agree on shared limits on how far they train models.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short ETH with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
So Ethereum is moving.
The plan replaces elliptic curves with hash-based cryptography, which rests on fewer structural assumptions about mathematics. It touches how users authorize transactions, how validators secure the network, and how layer-2 data gets verified. Drake proposed pulling the deadline from December 2029 to December 2028. Ethlabs withdrew its faster-block-production proposal from the Hegotá upgrade to free up engineers. The Foundation has deployed AI agents to hunt bugs in its own infrastructure, which is a reasonable response and also an admission about where the advantage currently sits.
Wedderburn’s own framing: it’s harder than the Merge, and there’s less time. He also acknowledged that moving faster makes it easier to ship bugs.
Bitcoin is on the same road. Blockstream’s Jonas Nick published a security analysis of SHRINCS last week, the apparent frontrunner to replace Bitcoin’s signatures, with sizes running from 548 bytes to 5,777 against today’s 64 to 71.
So the AI threat is looming (and accelerating), but the two largest crypto assets have teams that are responding. Now we wait on action, and more assurances that crypto is safe from AI threats. Assurances that could ensure the bottom is in fact in, if and when they arrive…

Bitcoin ETFs near $5B in record monthly outflows amid AI stock rout
US spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded $4.94 billion in November net outflows, exceeding the previous monthly record of $4.51 billion set in June.
US-listed spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) are approaching $5 billion in monthly net outflows for the first time since their launch in January 2024.
The funds recorded $231.6 million in net outflows on Tuesday, extending their withdrawal streak to six consecutive trading days, according to SoSoValue. November outflows reached $4.94 billion, surpassing the previous monthly record of $4.51 billion in June.
The latest withdrawals bring net outflows for 2026 to about $4.57 billion, erasing the recovery that saw the funds attract $6.34 billion in the third quarter.
Digital asset investment company Teroxx identified rising interest rates and weakness in AI stocks among the factors behind declining ETF demand in its November research report, noting that markets increasingly expect another Federal Reserve rate hike in December.
“In the near term, flows into Bitcoin will remain under pressure as long as artificial intelligence stocks are searching for a bottom and the December Fed decision looms,” Teroxx digital asset researcher Leonardo Larieira said in comments shared with Cointelegraph.
Larieira said a sustained recovery in Bitcoin ETF inflows would require long-term US Treasury yields to stabilize. “Once that happens, returning institutional capital will meet a regulated infrastructure that is far deeper than it was in August,” he added.

articles.title: French Senate Rejects Plan to Make Crypto Holders Declare Self-Custody Wallets
articles.text:
In brief
- France's Senate rejected amendments that would have required taxpayers to declare self-custodied crypto worth more than €100,000 ($110,000) during its 2027 budget debate.
- Public accounts minister David Amiel argued existing EU reporting rules already bring transparency, and that a simple declaration would not help track money laundering or fraud.
- Senators also rejected proposals to tax swaps from crypto into stablecoins and to extend France's exit tax to large crypto holdings.
France's Senate has rejected a proposal that would have required crypto holders to declare self-custodied wallets worth more than €100,000 ($110,000) to tax authorities, according to the official record of Tuesday's debate on the 2027 budget.
Two identical amendments, one from the Communist-led CRCE-K group and one from a group of senators led by Anne-Sophie Romagny, were voted down after both the government and the Senate's finance committee opposed them. The vote was earlier reported by Cointelegraph.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
The amendments would have obliged holders to declare self-custodied crypto above the threshold. French taxpayers already have to declare crypto accounts held on platforms, but not crypto held in their own wallets.
"The shop window is illuminated, but the back room remains in the dark," CRCE-K senator Alexandre Basquin said, in comments translated from French. The more closely platforms are monitored, the greater the incentive for large holders to keep their crypto themselves, he argued.
Minister for Public Action and Accounts David Amiel said the EU's DAC8 directive, which requires crypto service providers to report users' transactions to tax authorities, had already brought transparency. A purely declarative obligation would not let authorities track how crypto is used in money laundering or tax fraud cases, he said.
Second defeat
The proposal had already passed through France's lower house. The National Assembly's finance committee backed it in October, prompting a backlash from the crypto industry.
The budget was later rejected in the lower house, so the Senate is debating the government's original bill, without the crypto amendments that deputies had added.
BTC price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
On Tuesday, senators also rejected an amendment that would have made swaps from crypto into stablecoins a taxable event. Amiel argued that stablecoins are not money, as they have no legal tender status and are often unstable. A proposal to extend France's exit tax to crypto holdings worth more than €800,000 ($877,000) was also defeated.
Wrench attacks in France
Critics of the reporting plan had warned that a register of large crypto holders could become a target in France, which has become the global epicenter of "wrench attacks," in which criminals use violence to force victims to hand over crypto.
France's national anti-organized crime prosecutor's office recorded more than 70 crypto-linked kidnappings and unlawful detentions in the first eight months of 2026, Decrypt reported in September. Authorities charged 88 people, including minors, in a crackdown in April.
Leaks of personal data have added to those fears. A breach of France's tax authority in August exposed records tied to more than 678,000 people and businesses. In January, a tax agent was accused of looking up crypto investors and prison guards in tax databases for an unidentified buyer, Le Parisien reported, while a June attack in Nancy followed a data breach at French crypto tax platform Waltio.

articles.title: Bitcoin Could Fall Below $53.2K if Bear-Market History Repeats
articles.text:
Bitcoin price may fall below $53K if bear-market history repeats
Bitcoin price downside targets focused on the $53,200 realized price as research saw pointed to bear-market patterns continuing for BTC/USD.
Bitcoin (BTC) is approaching investors’ aggregate cost basis, with previous bear markets pointing to the risk of further price declines.
Key points:
- Bitcoin traded at $58,919 at 10 am UTC on Wednesday, 10.75% above its realized price of $53,200.
- BTC/USD fell below its realized price before every previous bear-market bottom, trading below it for up to 301 days.
- Relative to capital inflows, Bitcoin’s onchain realized losses hit their highest levels since the FTX implosion in November 2022.
Bitcoin targets realized price for first time in four years
New research from onchain analytics platform Glassnode shows BTC/USD now trades just 10% above its realized price.
Realized price represents the average price at which each Bitcoin last moved onchain. When the spot price falls below this level, currently around $53,200, holders are collectively sitting on an unrealized loss.
BTC/USD one-week chart with realized price. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
During prior bear markets, Bitcoin fell through its realized price before establishing its next long-term floor.
“In each of those bear markets, however, price ended up well below the Realized Price,” Glassnode wrote in the latest edition of its The Week Onchain newsletter.
During Bitcoin’s last bear market in 2022, price spent 180 days below realized price before reclaiming it in January 2023. The record for time spent below investors’ aggregate cost basis is 301 days across 2014 and 2015, per calculations from Bitfinex Alpha, the research arm of crypto exchange Bitfinex.
Applying previous declines below realized price to today’s level would put Bitcoin at about $45,000 in a repeat of the March 2020 crash, or around $41,000 and $37,000 using the 2022 and 2018 bear-market lows, respectively.
“Should this time not be different after all, we would expect price to go lower and close below the Realized Price, which is a little over 10% away,” Glassnode added.
Bitcoin realized price comparison. Source: Glassnode
Realized losses reflect start of “capitulation”
Both older and younger investor cohorts continue to realize losses onchain following Bitcoin’s fall Saturday to its lowest level since September 2024.

Glassnode noted that relative to capital inflows, aggregate onchain losses now run at their highest level since the end of the 2022 bear market during the implosion of crypto exchange FTX — a sign that “capitulation has begun.”

articles.title: Florida Man Jailed for Using AI to Pose as Streamer N3ON in $260K Crypto Scam
articles.text:
In brief
- A Florida man was sentenced to 47 months in prison for impersonating streamer N3ON, including with an AI-cloned voice, to take $260,000 from a meme coin project.
- David Anthony Sanchez, 36, posed as both N3ON and his representative, signed agreements in the streamer's name and sent a fake voice recording confirming the deal.
- He pleaded guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, and was ordered to pay restitution, after converting much of the crypto into dollars.
A Port St. Lucie, Florida, man has been sentenced to 47 months in federal prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate popular streamer N3ON and con a meme coin project's organizers out of roughly $260,000 in crypto.
David Anthony Sanchez, 36, who also went by "Dave the Jewler" and other aliases, was sentenced by U.S. District Judge Melissa Damian after pleading guilty to money laundering and aggravated identity theft, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida said on Tuesday. He was also ordered to pay restitution to his victims.
A Port St. Lucie man was sentenced to 47 months in federal prison for using artificial intelligence to impersonate a popular online streamer and deceive investors in a cryptocurrency fraud scheme that caused approximately $260,000 in losses. The case serves as a warning that… pic.twitter.com/4DZnaiaPNt
— US Attorney's Office Southern District of Florida (@USAO_SDFL) November 24, 2026
According to court records, Sanchez set up online accounts made to look as though they belonged to N3ON, and contacted the organizers of a crypto meme coin project while posing as both the streamer and his representative.
He signed agreements using N3ON's identity and sent the organizers an AI-generated voice recording that mimicked the streamer, falsely confirming that N3ON would endorse, promote and take part in the project, prosecutors said. Believing the deal was real, the organizers sent about $260,000 in crypto to accounts Sanchez controlled.
Sanchez then converted much of the crypto into U.S. dollars through transactions designed to hide where the money came from and who owned it, and spent it on himself, according to prosecutors. The press release did not name the meme coin project.
"The defendant exploited artificial intelligence to manipulate the trust of unsuspecting victims and deprive them of their money," Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas said in a statement.

The same tactics have been used to target crypto workers.

Legislation aimed at the problem has stalled. The AI Fraud Deterrence Act, introduced by Reps. Ted Lieu (D-CA) and Neal Dunn (R-FL) in November 2025, would raise penalties for AI-assisted fraud.
AI-assisted money laundering, one of the charges Sanchez pleaded guilty to, would carry fines of up to $1 million or three times the value of the transaction, alongside up to 20 years in prison. The bill has not advanced beyond the House Judiciary Committee.

articles.title: HYPE Down 40% From Peak as Trump Bump Fades
articles.text:
HYPE drops 8% as Trump bump gives way to 40% slide from peak
HYPE traded below its price before Trump’s August remarks as wallets linked to Abraxas Capital reportedly exited the Hyperliquid platform.
Hyperliquid’s native token HYPE fell nearly 8% on Wednesday, trading below its price before US President Donald Trump’s remarks on US access to the exchange.
CoinGecko data showed HYPE (HYPE) at $58.14, about 40% below its Sept. 23 all-time high of $97.96. The token traded around $62 immediately before Trump’s remarks.
On Aug. 19, Trump said that Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chair Michael Selig was working to bring Hyperliquid into the US. On Oct. 29, HYPE surged toward its record high after Intercontinental Exchange, owner of the NYSE, said it would seek approval for regulated Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures aimed at US retail traders.
Hyperliquid is a decentralized trading platform and layer-1 blockchain best known for its onchain perpetual futures exchange.
HYPE rallied from early-2026 lows near $20 to its September record as Hyperliquid expanded into markets beyond crypto. Its HIP-3 upgrade, live since October 2025, lets those who meet staking requirements deploy perpetual markets for a wide range of assets.
Related: Hong Kong adds Hyperliquid to list of ‘suspicious’ crypto platforms
Wallets linked to Abraxas Capital exit Hyperliquid
Meanwhile, blockchain analytics account Lookonchain reported that wallets labeled by Arkham as belonging to Abraxas Capital exited Hyperliquid.
Lookonchain said the wallets sold 219,081 HYPE (about $13.25 million) and then bought 4,230 ETH ($7.09 million).
Cointelegraph reached out to Abraxas Capital to confirm the wallet attribution and reported exit but did not receive a response before publication.
Abraxas Capital Management was founded in 2002 and has specialized in digital assets since 2017. The London-based company is regulated by the UK Financial Conduct Authority.
Stablecoin giant Tether is a major investor in Abraxas’ flagship Elysium fund, according to court filings made public in July. Abraxas co-founder Fabio Frontini testified that Tether’s stake reached about $800 million, roughly 75% of the fund’s assets at the time.
Magazine: AI agents are using credit cards. Where does that leave crypto?

articles.title: Hyperliquid Leads Altcoin Losses as Bitcoin Slips Below $59K
articles.text:
In brief
- Hyperliquid's HYPE fell more than 8% in 24 hours, the steepest drop among the top 20 cryptocurrencies, after investment firm Abraxas Capital closed its positions on the exchange.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have shed $4.94 billion in November, their worst month on record, after six straight days of outflows.
- Options traders hold the most downside protection relative to bets on gains since May 2021, and dealer hedging could amplify swings between $58,000 and $64,000, Glassnode said.
Hyperliquid's HYPE token led crypto's latest leg down on Wednesday, as one of the exchange's most profitable traders shut down its operations there.
HYPE fell 8.2% over 24 hours to $57.86, the steepest drop among the 20 largest cryptocurrencies by market cap, and is down 15.8% over the past week, according to Decrypt data. Bitcoin slipped 1.7% over the same period to $58,801, and Ethereum lost 2.4%, extending a sell-off that has spread across risk assets.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short HYPE with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Abraxas exits Hyperliquid
Abraxas Capital has withdrawn its remaining funds from Hyperliquid and closed its entire book, almost two years after it started trading there, pseudonymous onchain analyst MLM said on Telegram on Tuesday.
The firm traded $13.4 billion on Hyperliquid and made $530 million, including at least $67 million from funding payments, according to MLM. The positions were one leg of a market-neutral strategy for its Elysium Global Arbitrage Fund, the analyst said.
Two Hyperliquid accounts labeled as Abraxas Capital on analytics platform Hyperdash have recorded combined all-time profits of more than $550 million, and now hold just over $5,000 between them, Hyperdash data shows. On Tuesday, the two accounts unstaked about 219,000 HYPE, worth roughly $12.7 million at current prices, and sent it elsewhere.
"With HYPE, upcoming token unlocks could be adding extra pressure," Eric Andersson, co-founder of Byrrgis, told Decrypt. "Altcoins tend to get hit even harder in these situations."
Record ETF outflows
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $231.6 million in net outflows on Tuesday, their sixth consecutive day of withdrawals, according to SoSoValue data. Outflows over those six trading days total $2.6 billion.
That takes November's net outflows to $4.94 billion, surpassing June 2026's $4.51 billion as the funds' worst month since they launched in January 2024. Total net assets stand at $72 billion.
Andersson pointed to ETF outflows, uncertainty over interest rates, liquidations and weaker sentiment across financial markets as drivers of Bitcoin's decline.
BTC price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
Options traders brace for more
Options traders have turned increasingly bearish. Over the past week, 1.7 put options, which pay out when prices fall, changed hands for every call on a seven-day average, the most since June 2022, Glassnode said in its weekly report. Measured by open interest, the ratio is at its highest since May 2021.
Bitcoin is back at its summer lows near $60K, and stocks are also in a downtrend.
BTC gave back the whole NVIDIA rally in less than six hours, an indication of severe relative weakness.
More on capitulation and leverage in this week's Week On-chain. https://t.co/GwEUc1pqHW
— glassnode (@glassnode) November 24, 2026
Such readings do not always mark a bottom. In June 2022, a similar reading coincided with a price low, but the bear market's final low was still five months away, while the open interest peak in April 2021 came near a market top, Glassnode noted.
Glassnode also said options dealers are "short gamma" between $58,000 and $64,000, meaning their hedging requires them to sell as prices fall and buy as they rise, which can make moves in either direction larger. Just outside that range, their hedging would slow a move, the firm said.
Glassnode's report found that Bitcoin investors are locking in their heaviest losses since the collapse of FTX.
A clearer outlook on interest rates and renewed ETF inflows could help bring stability back to the market, Andersson said.

articles.title: French Senate Rejects 100K euro Crypto Wallet Reporting Proposal
articles.text:
French Senate rejects 100K euro crypto wallet disclosure requirement
Senators also rejected stablecoin-swap and crypto exit-tax proposals, while the 2027 budget remains under parliamentary consideration.
The French Senate rejected proposals Tuesday that would have required taxpayers to declare self-custodied crypto holdings worth at least 100,000 euros (about $109,600) to tax authorities.
Senators voted down identical amendments from Pascal Savoldelli and Anne-Sophie Romagny during debate on the 2027 budget. The requirement would have applied when the combined value of crypto held in wallets outside a service provider reached at least 100,000 euros on Dec. 31.
The reporting requirement was initially adopted by the National Assembly on Nov. 3, but fell when lawmakers rejected the budget’s entire revenue section on Nov. 4.
Budget Minister David Amiel opposed the wallet-reporting amendments, saying they would not enable authorities to track how crypto is used, particularly in money laundering or tax fraud. The Senate’s finance committee followed the government’s recommendation to reject them.
Requiring a declaration of wallet holdings without a taxable event would amount to “placing a blanket suspicion on good-faith users,” Faustine Fleuret, global head of public affairs at lending protocol Morpho, told Cointelegraph.
She said that self-custodial wallet reporting would create “unequal treatment” compared to other assets like jewelry or fine art, “whose mere holding is not subject to a reporting obligation in the absence of a taxable transaction.”
Related: Lagarde warns Europe could miss chance to unify tokenized markets
Senate rejects stablecoin tax and crypto exit tax
The Senate also rejected another amendment from Savoldelli that would have taxed gains on crypto conversions into stablecoins classified as electronic-money tokens under EU rules. It would have applied from Jan. 1, 2027.
The Assembly adopted a similar amendment from MP Nicolas Sansu on Oct. 16, but that measure also fell when the Assembly rejected the revenue section. Savoldelli reintroduced the proposal on Nov. 19 before Tuesday’s rejection.
A proposal to extend France’s exit tax to unrealized crypto gains when qualifying taxpayers moved their tax residence abroad also failed. The Assembly rejected similar proposals on Oct. 30.
Another crypto-related amendment remains pending. Senator Thomas Dossus’s amendment would raise a proposed fine for refusing tax authorities’ information requests from 10,000 euros to 50,000 euros per request. It would cover financial institutions, crypto service providers and platform operators.
The Senate is scheduled to complete debate and vote on the budget’s revenue section Saturday, with Sunday available if needed.
A Senate vote on the full budget is scheduled for Dec. 9. The rejected crypto measures are absent from the text as it stands, but the budget still faces further negotiations before final adoption.
Magazine: Made an ‘honest’ mistake with crypto taxes? New bill offers way out

articles.title: USDT Market Cap Falls $9B in Largest 60-Day Drop Since 2022
articles.text:
Stablecoin redemptions hit $12B in 30 days, echoing 2022 bear market
Crypto research firm Kaiko said the cash-out was smaller than in 2022 and has slowed, with stablecoin supply down just 0.4% since Nov. 13.
Net redemptions across the 11 stablecoins tracked by crypto research firm Kaiko reached about $12 billion in the 30 days to Nov. 13, echoing a pattern analysts saw during the 2022 bear market.
Tether’s USDt (USDT) and Circle’s USDC (USDC), the two largest stablecoins, each ended the period with about 4% fewer tokens in circulation. Since Nov. 13, total stablecoin supply has fallen just 0.4%, while USDC supply has edged higher.
“The contraction looks like capital leaving crypto rather than rotating within it,” Kaiko analyst Andrew Yang told Cointelegraph.
Yang said that the redemptions left traders with fewer stablecoins on hand to buy crypto.
The cash-out coincided with outflows from US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds and a shift in expectations toward tighter Federal Reserve policy.
USDT trading slows while onchain transfers hold up
Daily trading volume in USDT pairs was about half its 2025 average over the past month, according to Kaiko. Bitcoin (BTC) market makers continued to post orders close to the market price.
The dollar value of orders to buy or sell Bitcoin within 1% of its market price fell about 15% over the past month. Measured in Bitcoin, those orders were 9% larger in aggregate, Yang said.
Related: Stablecoin supply falls $14.2B in biggest 30-day drop since June 2022
Nearly 90% of the 30-day decline in stablecoin supply came from Ethereum, a major hub for exchanges and decentralized finance. On Tron, a network more commonly used for payments, stablecoin supply fell just 1.4%, according to Kaiko.
Onchain transfers of USDT and USDC have averaged about $157 billion a day so far this quarter. That’s above the 2025 daily average of $130 billion, though below the pace in the fourth quarter of last year, Kaiko said.
How the cash-out compares with 2022
During the 2022–2023 bear market, rising interest rates and falling crypto prices drove months of redemptions from fiat-backed stablecoins, Yang said. He described the current pullback as much smaller and pointed to a more recent comparison. Stablecoin supply fell from mid-May into June this year before stabilizing in August.
For USDT, the latest decline is the largest since 2022, said Julio Moreno, head of research at blockchain analytics firm CryptoQuant. Its market capitalization has fallen $9 billion over the past 60 days, a drop Moreno linked to a broader retreat from risk assets, including stocks and commodities.
Source: CryptoQuant
Moreno tracks USDT supply as a measure of the funds available for trading. Exchanges hold 51% of the USDT circulating on Ethereum, he told Cointelegraph.
USDT supply was also shrinking when Bitcoin bottomed in November 2022, Moreno said.
He said stablecoin supply would have to grow again “in order for liquidity to improve and the market to recover.”
Magazine: Private, fast USDT is coming to Bitcoin. Can it compete with Ethereum and Tron?

articles.title: Take-Two Hits GTA 6 PC Port Leonida With DMCA, Taking Down 3,007 GitHub Repos
articles.text:
In brief
- Take-Two filed a DMCA notice against Leonida, a GitHub project to run the leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 on PC, and GitHub removed 3,007 repositories.
- Take-Two said the project's instruction to "bring your own files" was "intentionally misleading," given its timing and focus on the leaked game.
- The project's creator also received a copyright strike from Discord, but has since hinted that "something's coming soon."
Take-Two Interactive has used a copyright takedown notice to remove Leonida, one of the most prominent projects attempting to port the leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 to PC, along with thousands of copies of its code.
GitHub published a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) notice from Take-Two's IP Enforcement Team on Tuesday. Because the publisher alleged that all or most of the project's forks infringed to the same extent as the original, GitHub said it processed the takedown against the entire network of 3,007 repositories.
The notice clears up why the project disappeared on Monday. Its GitHub page had shown an error page rather than a DMCA notice, so it was initially unclear whether it had been removed by its creator or by Take-Two.
The project described itself as "a native PC recompilation of the Xbox version of Grand Theft Auto 6." Take-Two said it reproduced copyrighted elements of the game and was a derivative work, breaching Rockstar's terms of service, which bar users from decompiling, reverse engineering or creating derivative works from its games.
'Bring your own files'
Leonida did not include the leaked game files itself. Instead, its instructions told users to supply their own Xbox Series files.
Take-Two dismissed that approach. Stolen files from an Xbox Series build of the game were publicly distributed on November 20, 2026, and Leonida's repository opened the following day, it said.
#1 Searched Person on Google 2026?
"The instruction to 'bring your own files' attempts to shift the responsibility for supplying files to the user and to make it seems as if this is a general-purpose project," Take-Two wrote. "This is intentionally misleading."
The timing and the project's "explicit focus" on Grand Theft Auto showed the files users needed were the leaked ones, and that its developers knew it, Take-Two added. It asked GitHub to disable the repository and all its forks.
Take-Two has made the same argument before. On November 18, GitHub published four Take-Two notices against unofficial ports of GTA V to mobile devices, Macs and web browsers, three of which told users to supply their own game files. In each, Take-Two said such disclaimers "do not automatically shield" developers from secondary copyright liability when they knowingly facilitate infringement.
Discord strike
The project's pseudonymous creator also posted a screenshot of a Discord notice saying his server had broken the platform's rules on copyright infringement, limiting his access to servers until November 30, 2026.
He later tweeted that he was no longer working on the project "because of T2," but that "there are and always will be more projects." On Wednesday, he told followers to ignore his earlier posts, adding: "Something's coming soon."
Ignore my other posts. Something’s coming soon 👀
— NotRexed (@ItsNotRexed) November 25, 2026
The takedown follows the release of the build's main executable by leaker Cyberleek on Monday. Cyberleek had promised to release the file if the CYBERLEEK meme coin reached a $15 million market cap. The token fell short, but Cyberleek released the file anyway, and porting projects expected a playable version within days.
Take-Two has pursued the leaks for months, subpoenaing Discord and Microsoft, which owns GitHub, in August for data that could help identify Cyberleek. Rockstar has not announced a PC version of GTA 6.

articles.title: EU Plans AI and Quantum Computing Fund of Up to $55B: Report
articles.text:
EU seeks up to $55B for AI and quantum computing fund: Report
Hackers already use AI to target crypto exchanges, while future quantum computers could break the cryptography that protects users’ funds.
The European Union is planning a fund that could raise up to 50 billion euros ($54.7 billion) to invest in artificial intelligence and quantum computing companies, the Financial Times reported Wednesday.
The EU wants to reduce its reliance on US and Chinese technology. Two officials involved in the talks told the Financial Times that the proposed Sovereign Tech Equity Fund would invest larger sums, take on more risk and hold its stakes longer than existing EU financing programs.
According to the report, the European Commission aims to attract private investors, targeting up to six euros in investment for every euro committed. Operational details are expected in February.
The two technologies the EU wants to back pose different risks for crypto holders. Hackers are already using AI to target crypto exchanges and steal funds, while a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could one day let attackers access someone else’s crypto.
On Nov. 4, India’s national cybersecurity agency warned that hackers were using AI tools to target crypto exchanges and other financial firms, with attacks resulting in stolen wallet keys and drained funds.
In September, European financial regulators warned that quantum computers could undermine the cryptographic systems securing blockchain transactions. The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) warned Thursday that upgrading blockchains to withstand quantum attacks could reduce transaction throughput and increase fees.
Related: ECB warns legislative delays could postpone digital euro launch

articles.title: South Korea’s Crypto Bill Could Reshape Its Stablecoin Race
articles.text:
South Korea’s crypto bill could move stablecoin race beyond token issuance
South Korea’s draft bill favors bank-led stablecoin issuance but allows fintech and technology companies to become the largest individual shareholders.
South Korean fintech companies could gain influence in bank-led stablecoin groups by signing up partners that help people spend won-denominated tokens, Tiger Research said in its Tuesday report.
“Those relationships are likely to matter more to the business than the volume of stablecoins issued,” the Asia-focused research company said.
On Tuesday, South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) unveiled its draft digital assets bill that would initially limit issuance of won-denominated stablecoins to consortiums in which banks collectively hold a majority stake. A fintech or technology company could still hold a larger stake than any individual bank.
The proposal follows months of regulatory disagreements. The Bank of Korea has advocated for bank-led issuance, citing monetary policy and financial stability risks, while the FSC previously favored allowing nonbank companies to issue stablecoins.
If the Banking Act’s 15% limit on a bank’s stake in a nonfinancial company applies to stablecoin issuers, at least four banks would need to join each consortium to secure a majority, according to Tiger Research.
Stablecoin opportunities extend beyond domestic issuance
Vincent Chok, founder and CEO of First Digital, whose subsidiary issues the FDUSD stablecoin, told Cointelegraph that bank-majority consortiums could give won-denominated stablecoins credibility at launch, while fintech participation could help preserve innovation.
“Beyond who issues, Korea’s ability to capture the wider economic activity around stablecoins will rest on efficient on- and off-ramps and rails connecting KRW with global dollar liquidity,” Chok said.
South Korean financial and technology companies have already started exploring these opportunities. In May, KB Financial Group completed a won-denominated stablecoin pilot covering merchant payments and cross-border remittances. In July, Viva Republica, which operates the Toss payments app, partnered with Optimism and Sunnyside Labs to test stablecoin-based payments for financial institutions.
Related: How South Korea’s proposed 20% cap could change who runs Upbit
The bill still needs to pass the National Assembly before proceeding to presidential promulgation. Tiger Research said the legislation is expected to take effect one year after promulgation, while key details, including shareholder requirements for stablecoin consortiums, remain subject to subsequent enforcement decrees.
Magazine: How to preserve wealth and access funds during a national emergency

articles.title: Solana DEX Velocity Halts Transactions Over Bug
articles.text:
Solana DEX Velocity halts trading over bug just months after relaunch
Velocity relaunched in September as a rebuilt version of Drift Protocol, which was attacked by North Korean hackers in April.
Solana-based decentralized exchange Velocity said Wednesday it has suspended all transactions while its team works to fix a bug.
“User deposits are safe,” Velocity said in a post on X, and that the protocol would remain paused until it was safe to resume.
Velocity is the rebuilt, forked version of Drift Protocol, which was hacked in April. Velocity relaunched under the new name in September.
Unlike Drift Protocol, Velocity DEX focuses exclusively on perpetual futures trading, removing standalone spot trading. Data from DefiLlama shows its perp volume saw a significant spike in November, with the biggest spike in volume on Nov. 18 and 19.
Velocity said it will share more about the bug on social media.
Drift reported about $295 million in losses from an April 1 hack, which has been blamed on UNC6862, a North Korean threat group.
Related: Drift exploiter sends $61M ETH to Tornado Cash, holds $194M

articles.title: Crypto host who once promoted a $50 billion memecoin vision now tells traders to get out
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bullpen said the known impact was limited to 19 early beta accounts, including an account belonging to Ansem.
- Bullpen said taking over affected accounts exposed wallets the users had already imported into the trading app.
- Ansem urged Bullpen users to withdraw their funds until he could confidently say their money was safe.
Jonah, co-host of the 1000x podcast, wrote on Nov. 24 to “get out while you still can” after crypto trader Ansem said his wallet had been hacked.
Jonah predicted that staying in crypto would carry a stigma. At 03:07 UTC on Nov. 25, trading app Bullpen said the known impact of its breach was limited to 19 early beta accounts.
At 03:53 UTC, Ansem advised users to withdraw their funds until he could confidently say they were safe.
Ansem’s initial post said he suspected that someone had accessed the Bullpen profile where he had imported the private key for a Solana wallet he used on Pump.fun, and Jonah’s quote-post came in response to that claim.
Bullpen’s first public notice came later Tuesday and identified Ansem as one of the users affected.
What the beta accounts exposed
In its initial notice, Bullpen gave a preliminary range of 18 to 19 affected accounts, all opened between April and June 2024. The company said it took the affected test service offline.
Its Wednesday update gave a figure of 19 accounts and said it had seen no further movement of the funds at that point.
Bullpen said the attacker took over the older accounts, exposing wallets users had imported into them. For users who had imported a wallet, the access Bullpen described extended beyond the trading app to funds in that wallet.
The private key Ansem said he imported could authorize transfers from the wallet he used on Pump.fun. The company said 99.8% of the funds taken came from one account, which it did not name.
Bullpen added that it was working with the FBI and other authorities, along with the services involved, to freeze and recover the funds. Ansem said he tried to freeze the money while it was still in USDC, but the attempt required a court order.
The updates describe efforts to recover the money and leave the recovered amount undisclosed.
In his follow-up, Ansem said two of his Solana wallets were compromised, identifying them as the wallet he imported from Pump.fun and a wallet already on Bullpen.
He attributed the breach to a weakness in older accounts that he said let someone bypass Bullpen’s two-factor login. Ansem also said a separate BitGo wallet requiring multiple signatures, which he said held 49% of the ANSEM token supply, was safe and unmoved.
An ANSEM sell-off unfolded on Nov. 24, driven by a large ANSEM sell-off from a publicly labeled wallet. Bitquery reported about $2.57 million in USDC at one Arbitrum address at 17:00 UTC that day.
Jonah’s own crypto history comes up
Jonah’s comments drew a quote-post from user soby and a “This you?” reply from @CupOJoseph. In another reply, Jonah said he liked Ansem and had helped launch a token a couple of years earlier.
Jonah had published a BODEN roadmap in April 2024. The post imagined the memecoin listing on the New York Stock Exchange at a $50 billion valuation and becoming a reserve currency.
In a separate post early Wednesday, he distinguished between launching a token he considered worthless and selling it, which he said made someone a scammer.
In his own post Tuesday, 1000x co-host Avi Felman wrote that “crypto is fine,” arguing the industry grew stronger through previous downturns.

articles.title: Trump Leaves Door Open to Pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
articles.text:
Trump willing to pardon Jensen Huang, says it won’t be necessary
The president’s remarks come days before Jensen Huang is due to face congressional questioning over national security concerns and US chip export controls.
US President Donald Trump has left the door open to pardoning Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang, though he said he doesn’t think it’ll be necessary.
Trump made the comments during an interview with the New York Post just a day after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia’s CEO amid scrutiny over his affair with a suspected Chinese spy and whether he allowed the company’s chips to fall into China’s hands.
Asked about a pardon for any potential crimes, Trump told The Post: “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”
Trump had earlier claimed credit for pushing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back — a move which saw Nvidia’s stock surge on Monday.
Huang is scheduled to testify before lawmakers in a closed-door, transcribed interview with the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the House Intelligence Committee and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party on Dec. 1.
On Dec. 3, Huang is set to be the sole witness in a hearing by the Committee on Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs about US export controls.
Related: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO amid ongoing intelligence probe

articles.title: Lido tightens Ethereum staking penalties as operators gain access to larger validators
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Lido voters backed a wider penalty mandate covering both community staking modules in a Nov. 23 signaling vote.
- Lido’s automatic bond deduction covered about 43% of the March slashing losses, and the operator voluntarily paid the rest.
- If a penalty exceeds an operator’s available bond, the unpaid amount becomes debt recoverable from future rewards or top-ups.
Lido voters backed a proposal on Nov. 23 to let the committee overseeing its two community staking modules recover more Ethereum staking losses from operators’ bonds.
In the March slashing case that prompted the vote, Lido’s contracts automatically recovered about 43% of the loss, while the operator voluntarily covered the rest.
The Snapshot result posted on Lido’s governance forum showed 53.8 million LDO in favor and 4.1 million against, enough to reach quorum. The off-chain vote backed a wider remit for the committee overseeing Lido’s two open-entry Community Staking Modules, 0x01 and 0x02.
The vote carried zero on-chain actions, so individual penalties must still be reported and settled separately.
The updated mandate extends an existing penalty mechanism used when operators divert block rewards. It would also cover staking rewards missed after slashing, along with incidents that could harm the protocol, such as withdrawal delays or risks to validator key security.
Committee members who backed the change called for documented evidence, credit for losses already recovered, and a chance for operators to respond.
Lido’s final incident report put the March 12 slashing at 0.7973122 ETH in penalties and missed rewards. When the six validators withdrew, Lido’s contracts automatically took 0.3459189 ETH from the operator’s bond to cover the withdrawal shortfall.
The operator voluntarily paid the remaining 0.4513933 ETH after the committee made contact, and Lido reported that the incident was fully resolved in April.
In a similar case under the wider mandate, the committee could assess the missed rewards separately and lock collateral against that amount. The amount Lido could collect at settlement would depend on the bond left after the automatic deduction.
Under the penalty procedure, the report locks the assessed loss and any applicable fine, and the operator can compensate Lido or dispute the report. The committee can start an Easy Track motion to settle the penalty.
The locked collateral is burned when the motion is enacted, and Lido’s Easy Track rules give LDO holders at least 72 hours to object. Objections backed by at least 0.5% of total LDO supply stop the motion.
How much Ethereum the operator’s bond can cover
The bond backs all validators run under the same operator account in a module. Lido sizes the required collateral by the number of keys the operator runs.
In 0x01, a default operator posts 2.4 ETH for the first 32 ETH validator and 1.3 ETH for each additional key. The 0x02 module requires 32 ETH for the first key and 30 ETH for each additional key.
A 0x02 validator receives 32 ETH to start and can receive more stake after activation without increasing the required bond.
At the theoretical 2,048 ETH effective-balance ceiling, the 32 ETH first-key bond would equal about 1.56% of that balance. The 2.4 ETH first-key bond in 0x01 equals 7.5% of the validator’s 32 ETH balance.
Lido launched 0x02 on Oct. 23, and its October operator update reported nearly 800,000 ETH being validated in the established module. The first 30 keys in 0x02 had received seed deposits, or 960 ETH in all, with 54 more keys still queued at the time.
Kvorum’s record of a separate Nov. 18 motion shows the 0x02 allocation limit rose from 0.01% to 0.5% of Lido’s core pool. The higher limit lets the module take on more stake as deposits arrive.
Lido’s operator documentation says the collateral is held in stETH. If an assessed penalty exceeds the available bond, the excess becomes debt that can be recovered from future rewards or bond top-ups.
Queued keys that lose bond coverage stop receiving deposits, and unbonded validators can face exit requests. How much and how quickly the protocol can recover depends on what the operator has left in the bond and what comes in later.

articles.title: Bitcoin Lightning operators could recover stuck payments even after losing channel data
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Core Lightning’s 26.12 release candidate adds a manual tool for recovering eligible pending funds after channel data loss.
- Outgoing funds can be reclaimed after expiry if the matching output on the closing transaction remains unspent.
- An incoming claim needs the matching preimage and must confirm before the peer reclaims the same output.
Core Lightning’s first 26.12 release candidate adds a way to reclaim funds from some pending Bitcoin Lightning payments.
It applies after an operator loses local channel data and a peer closes the channel by posting a transaction to Bitcoin. The tool gives the operator separate ways to reclaim outgoing funds or collect incoming funds, depending on the payment information that survived.
Core Lightning published the test build on Nov. 18, and still headed the project’s release list on Nov. 25 as a pre-release.
Bitcoin Optech covered the feature in its Nov. 20 newsletter and revisited it in its Nov. 24 podcast recap.
Core Lightning’s existing recovery process can reclaim the operator’s main channel balance when the peer posts a closing transaction the recovering node has never seen.
The change adds a new tool that addresses a separate output: the amount the closing transaction sets aside for a payment that was still pending.
Which pending Bitcoin payments qualify
Both recovery paths require a matching output in the closing transaction that remains unspent. For a payment the operator offered, the tool’s manual says the operator needs the payment hash and the expiry. Once the timelock expires, the operator can reclaim those funds.
For a payment the peer offered, the operator needs the preimage, the secret that matches the payment hash. The operator’s claim must be confirmed on Bitcoin before the peer reclaims the same output. Once the timelock expires, the peer can take the funds back.
The tool reconstructs the spending conditions for each payment the operator wants to recover and checks them against the closing transaction, and skips payments that are too small to have an output.
It produces signed transactions for the operator to review and broadcast manually.
The operator needs the original node secret, the peer’s closing transaction, channel identifiers and key information, and details for each payment they want to recover.
A cooperating peer can supply the public commitment point tied to the closing transaction while keeping its private keys and commitment secrets private.
Core Lightning’s wallet recovery guide describes using the node secret and an emergency channel backup to reclaim the main balance after a peer closes the channel.
It also warns that restoring an outdated database can permanently lose funds, so recovering a pending payment depends on having enough information to reconstruct its particular output.

articles.title: CleanSpark Mulls Selling More Bitcoin Than It Mines
articles.text:
CleanSpark weighs selling more Bitcoin than it mines to de-risk books
The Bitcoin miner sold 2,102 BTC while it produced just 1,708 BTC in the September quarter.
Bitcoin miner CleanSpark is considering selling more Bitcoin than it mines each quarter to reduce its treasury risk, according to chief financial officer Gary Vecchiarelli, potentially further drawing down its holdings, last valued at $806 million.
CleanSpark held 13,530 Bitcoin at the end of September after mining 1,708 Bitcoin and selling 2,102 Bitcoin during the quarter, according to Cointelegraph’s tally of the company’s monthly operating updates. It marks the first time since at least 2024 that the company ended the quarter with less Bitcoin than it began with.
During a Q4 earnings call on Tuesday, Vecchiarelli said CleanSpark already aims to sell virtually all of the Bitcoin it mines to cover day-to-day operating costs, and told an analyst that selling slightly more than it produces in a quarter was one way to reduce treasury risk.
“We see the selling of a small amount of Bitcoin in excess of the quarterly production to be one way of de-risking,” said Vecchiarelli.
“But again, we are going to be sensitive and very reactionary to markets, and we are going to use that capital to make sure that we prevent dilution or bringing additional debt just to grow the company,” he said.
The remarks came as CleanSpark recorded a $987 million net loss for the fiscal year ended Sept. 30, compared with a net income of $364 million a year earlier. The company attributed two-thirds of the swing to noncash adjustments in the value of its Bitcoin holdings, as Bitcoin’s price fell from about $114,100 to $83,600 over the fiscal year.
Related: Trump-linked American Bitcoin secures $150M credit line from FalconX
CleanSpark also said it sold an undisclosed amount of Bitcoin since September to raise cash for expected acquisitions, as Vecchiarelli said it continues to view its Bitcoin holdings as “a liquid source of non-dilutive capital.”
CleanSpark trims mining fleet as AI buildout advances
CleanSpark also cut about 25,000 machines from its Bitcoin mining fleet in the September quarter, bringing the number in operation to about 200,000.
Vecchiarelli said the reduction improved energy efficiency to 14.8 joules per terahash from 15.8 in the previous quarter, which he said should help CleanSpark stay profitable if mining conditions deteriorate ahead of the 2028 Bitcoin halving.
“Going forward, in terms of hash rate, that will probably fluctuate, but we will continue to mine so as long as it’s profitable.”
In Sandersville, Georgia, CleanSpark said its first AI data hall remains on track for the fourth quarter of 2027. CleanSpark said it expects to start unplugging miners at the site in late 2027 as the data center comes online, then decide whether to relocate or sell them.
CleanSpark shares dropped 7.5% on Tuesday ahead of the earnings release to $5.12 and are down 2.25% in after-hours trading.
The company recorded $576.5 million in total revenue in the full year, down 25% from the previous fiscal year. Adjusted EBITDA came in at a loss of $304.2 million for the year.
